title: The Five Mysteries by which the First Man Descends and Returns
arc: Five seemingly trifling human gestures — peace, salutation, kiss, right hand, laying-on-of-hands — are revealed as the great mystery of how Divine Truth descended into self-love and was raised again, and as the same pattern by which every redeemed soul is welcomed home.
reading:
The teaching opens with a question about five everyday courtesies that pass between people in the world: the peace, the greeting/salutation, the embrace or kiss, the offered right hand, and the chirotonia (the laying-on-of-hands by which a lord raises up someone humble and makes him a lord beneath him). The questioner asks: where do these come from, whose are they, what do they mean? The answer is the heart of the teaching: although these gestures appear small and trifling in the natural world, they are in truth great — they are the visible residue, in human custom, of the five mysteries by which the First Man went out to battle the realm of darkness and by which he was received back into the Aeon of Light. The gestures men exchange daily are correspondential ultimates of the cosmic drama of redemption.

The teaching then unfolds the same five mysteries on three discrete planes, and the reader is meant to see one process moving through all three. On the first plane, these are the five rites of departure: as Divine Truth (the First Man) is being sent forth from the Father of Greatness against the Enemy, the gods and angels in the Land of Light give him their peace; the Mother of Life gives him her right hand; she embraces him as he separates from her; he himself bows in worship before the God of Truth and entreats power to be saved; and finally the Mother of Life lays her hands upon his head, arming him, girding him strongly, and setting him to the contest. So equipped he descends into the Deep and prevails against the great powers and against Enmity itself. These five are not external decorations of the descent — they are the descent's interior structure: love sent (peace), power conferred (right hand), conjunction held in parting (embrace), submission of the descending Truth to the inmost Father (worship), and consecration of the warrior (laying-on-of-hands). Together they make Divine Truth fit to enter the mingling without being lost in it.

On the second plane, the same five repeat in reverse as the rites of return. When the First Man comes up out of the war, the very peace he carried down is the peace he carries up — it is one and the same peace, given to him by the Calling when he was first sent from the Father of Life and now received again on his ascent. The Living Spirit gives him the right hand and brings him up from the battle. The Father of Life and the Mother of the Living embrace him as he emerges from the Deep. He worships in the gaze of the God of Truth and of all the blessed aeons. And finally he receives the great chirotonia: he is set on his feet before the Father, the Lord of the All, who calls to him from on high — "Sit, my son, my firstborn, at my right hand until I make all his enemies a footstool under his feet" — and so he is ordained leader of his brothers in the new aeon. The descent's five gifts have become the ascent's five glorifications. The same gestures that armed him for battle now crown him in victory, because in the spiritual world the equipment of mission and the consummation of mission are one continuous act of conjunction with the Father.

On the third plane — and this is where the teaching turns toward every reader — the same five mysteries operate at the redemption of each soul. The Form of Light (the Virgin of Light, the redeeming likeness in which the Lord meets the dying) appears to the soul leaving the body. She draws the soul away from the darkness toward the light; she stills the man with her kiss and her stillness, separating him from the demons that held his body. In her likeness, in her icon, the heart that comes forth from the body is at peace. Then the angel who holds the prize stretches out his right hand, draws the soul up out of the depth of the body, and welcomes it in with the kiss and the embrace. The soul worships its Redeemer, who is the Form of Light. And finally, in the house of the Living, among the angels, it receives the crown of glory in life forever — the personal chirotonia by which the redeemed soul is itself made a lord. Here the five greetings of the cosmos are recapitulated as the five stations of every individual ascent: separation from the body, the upraising hand, the welcoming embrace, the worshipping recognition of the Redeemer, and the crowning into the new aeon.

The argument of the teaching as a whole is therefore this: what looks like ordinary social custom — peace exchanged, hands clasped, embraces given, bows performed, ordinations conferred — is in fact the surviving correspondential trace of how Divine Truth itself moves between heaven and the realm of self-love. The descent of the First Man, his ascent, and the redemption of every soul share one liturgy. Because these five gestures are great in their origin, they remain great wherever they are honestly enacted: every true peace given, every right hand offered, every embrace of love, every act of worship, every laying-on-of-hands by which the humble is raised, repeats in ultimates the very mysteries that brought Divine Truth down to fight the darkness and lifted it home again. The teaching invites the hearer to see that he himself, in receiving the Form of Light at the end, will pass through the same five mysteries the First Man passed through — and so he is already, in every honest greeting, rehearsing his own redemption.

Conjunction held across separation; the Mother's farewell, the Father and Mother's welcome, the Form of Light's stilling kiss that draws the soul from the demons
The descending Truth's submission to the inmost Father for power; the soul's recognition of its Redeemer as the Form of Light
Consecration: the Mother arming the First Man for the contest; the Father seating him at his right hand as firstborn ruler; the redeemed soul crowned in the new aeon
